findings.problem: «a» is the CLDR narrow form, but in UI copy it is rarely seen and it collides with the preposition «a», so «2 a» is ambiguous. Its only consumer, session-projection.ts:409, is the session drawer column. That column already renders minutes_spaced «59 min» (6) and weeks «52 sem» (6) within the ~7 budget, so the full noun adds no new overflow.
findings.note: «1 año» 5 / «10 años» 7 cells, within the drawer column’s ~7 (minutes_spaced).

findings.problem: es CLDR categories are one/many/other. `many` is omitted, so it falls back to `other`, and output is identical: with a unit symbol and no noun, «de» is never inserted, so many==other. Shipped mobile es is mixed (23 plurals with many, 14 without). Core relay ships explicit identical arms (relay.notifications.age.minutes).
suggested: optional: add `many {…}` identical to `other` if the mobile validator or reviewers want category parity

observations: Translator flagged risks, judged: (1) compact == spaced «hace # min»: accepted. «m» reads as metres; core relay.notifications.age.minutes ships «hace # min» in the same inbox row role; «hace 59 min» is 11 against the ~10 hint, 1 over a soft hint. (2) «Esta semana»: accepted. Under «Hoy»/«Ayer» it reads as "the rest of this week", and it matches shipped tui/ui/relay group_week and the desktop sidebar. (3) «2 a»: see F2.

Width: short.minutes «59 min» (6) and short.weeks «52 sem» (6) exceed the ~4 hint. Their slots already hold equal or wider es text: Team Bridge rowStamp falls back to a toLocaleDateString month-short date («15 nov», 6), and the drawer column holds minutes_spaced (~7). minutes_seconds / hours_minutes render «59 min 07 s» / «23 h 07 min» (11 vs en 7). The seconds/minutes stay zero-padded, so there is no tick jitter. All are the shortest correct forms, so I filed no finding. A rendered check of the running transcript item is recommended.

resolutions.note: Unambiguous; 5–7 cells for realistic counts, within the drawer column’s ~7. The added many arm is correct: CLDR es many = exact multiples of 10^6 and a noun follows, so «1.000.000 de años» per style guide §Plurals; 1.500.000 → other «1.500.000 años». Unreachable in practice, harmless.
